answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by binding each identity to a soulbound admission relic that cannot be transferred or reused. New accounts remain on a sandbox island with zero voting weight until the relic lock matures and peers review the join graph. Tightly clustered sign-ups trigger a violet alert, which freezes those accounts pending extra deposits. An attacker therefore pays locked capital, delay, and extra collateral for every extra identity, while an honest agent incurs that cost only once.
